key_insight: For pulmonary embolism risk stratification, medical records and cardiac biomarkers mattered more than vascular imaging-derived graph features, and vascular graphs did not improve prediction.
clinical_relevance: This suggests routine PE risk assessment may gain more from combining clinical data with cardiac biomarkers than from adding complex vascular graph models alone.
method: Compared tabular models using medical records and biomarkers.
Added vascular biomarkers extracted from CTPA to assess incremental value.
Tested graph neural networks on the pulmonary vascular tree representation.
evidence_signal: The study used a private dataset of 353 PE cases with complete data and found strong tabular baselines outperformed vascular biomarker and GNN approaches.
watch_item: The findings come from a single private cohort, so limited sample size and dataset-specific effects may affect generalizability.
paper_title: Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification from CTPA and Medical Records: Vascular Graphs Are Not All You Need
